questions.stem: According to collision theory, which two conditions must be met for a successful collision to occur?

options.text: Particles must be the same size and at the same temperature
Particles must collide with sufficient energy and the correct orientation
Particles must be in the gas phase and moving quickly
Particles must be dissolved in solution and heated

questions.explanation: Collision theory states that particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, and they must collide with the correct orientation for a reaction to occur.

questions.stem: What is the activation energy of a reaction?

options.text: The total energy released during the reaction
The energy lost as heat during collisions
The minimum energy that colliding particles need to react
The maximum energy particles can have

questions.explanation: Activation energy is the minimum energy that colliding particles must have in order for a successful reaction to occur. Collisions with less energy than this will not result in a reaction.

questions.stem: Why do not all collisions between reactant particles lead to a reaction?

options.text: Because some particles are too large to react
Because some collisions lack sufficient energy or have incorrect orientation
Because particles can only react once
Because only gas particles can undergo collisions

questions.explanation: Not all collisions are successful because some do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy barrier, and some have the wrong orientation for bonds to break and reform.

questions.stem: How does increasing the frequency of collisions between particles affect the rate of reaction?

options.text: It decreases the rate because particles bounce off each other
It has no effect on the rate
It increases the rate because there are more chances for successful collisions
It increases the activation energy

questions.explanation: More frequent collisions mean there are more chances per second for collisions with sufficient energy and correct orientation, so the rate of reaction increases.

questions.stem: A collision between reactant particles that results in a chemical reaction is called a:

options.text: Failed collision
Elastic collision
Successful collision
Thermal collision

questions.explanation: A successful collision is one where the particles collide with enough energy (at least the activation energy) and the correct orientation, resulting in a chemical reaction.

questions.stem: Using collision theory, why does increasing concentration increase the rate of reaction?

options.text: It increases the activation energy of the reaction
It makes particles move faster
There are more particles in a given volume, so collisions are more frequent
It changes the orientation of the particles

questions.explanation: Higher concentration means more reactant particles in the same volume. The particles are closer together, leading to more frequent collisions and therefore a faster rate.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between collision theory and reaction rate?

options.text: Any factor that increases the number of successful collisions per second will increase the rate
Only temperature affects the number of successful collisions
The rate depends only on how fast the particles move
Successful collisions only occur between gas particles

questions.explanation: The rate of reaction depends on the frequency of successful collisions. Any factor that increases the number of successful collisions per second (such as concentration, temperature, surface area, or a catalyst) will increase the rate.
